parameters.content:
## Store 6 · Review page

When the cards pile up, `/store status` or `/store page` gives you a private link to this page: every review queue, up to 100 waiting in each, with a tick box on each one and Approve or Reject for the lot.

**Page** checks the link's signature and expiry (`/store` signs it with your Slack signing secret), reads each queue's rows (the `rows` query per queue in system.json) and draws the page.

**Decide** doesn't approve anything itself. For each ticked item it reads the card from Slack, builds the same button tap Slack would send (with the card's own ticked boxes and dropdowns), signs it with your signing secret and sends it to that workflow's own webhook. So every decision runs through the workflow's own checks and writes, and the Slack card updates to match, exactly as if you'd pressed the button. Then it reads the queue again to report what's decided.

Reading cards needs the bot scopes `channels:history` (and `groups:history` for private channels). The manifest adds them.

parameters.responseBody: This link has expired or was changed. Run /store page in Slack for a new one.

nodes.name: Page decision
nodes.notes: The page posts up to 10 decisions at a time, with the link's signature.

nodes.name: Decide settings
nodes.notes: build.py writes queues. internal_url is how n8n reaches its own webhooks.

nodes.name: Get those rows
nodes.notes: Only rows still waiting come back, so a decision made in Slack meanwhile is skipped.

nodes.name: Read the card
nodes.notes: Why HTTP: the Slack node has no read-one-message operation. The card's blocks give the tap its ticked boxes and dropdowns. Queues that don't store the card's ts (collection copy) search the channel's last 200 messages for the button.

nodes.name: Sign the tap
nodes.notes: Signed with your Slack signing secret, as Slack would sign it.

nodes.name: Send the tap
nodes.notes: Why HTTP: the workflow's own Slack webhook, so the decision runs through its own checks. One at a time, 1.5 s apart, so its card updates land in order.

nodes.name: Let them finish
nodes.notes: Most workflows answer Slack first and decide after, so give the last one a moment before reading the queue again.

parameters.query: insert into store_activity (source, user_id, user_name, action, detail) values ('review page', $1, $2, $3, $4)
